results.content: ## July 1 – 3, 2026 · Valencia, Spain. Internet and Big Data in Economics and Social Sciences. #### ***AI, Internet Data and Computational Methods in Social Sciences***. **8th International Conference on Advanced Research Methods and Analytics**. 1 – 3 July, 2026 · Valencia, Spain. Research methods in economics and social sciences are evolving rapidly with the rise of **AI-driven analytics**, **Large Language Models (LLMs)**, and **causal machine learning**. The increasing availability of Internet and Big Data sources has enabled new forms of measurement, inference, and theory testing. As these sources, methods, and applications become more interdisciplinary, the **8th International Conference on Advanced Research Methods and Analytics (CARMA 2026)** provides a consolidated forum for researchers and practitioners to exchange ideas and advances on how emerging computational and data-intensive methods are applied to social and economic phenomena, and to discuss the opportunities and challenges they bring. Topics of interest include, but are not limited to, the following areas:. * **Internet and Big Data sources**. + Google Trends and Search Engine data. + Web scraping and online content analysis. + Geospatial, sensor, and mobile phone data. + Multimodal and heterogeneous data integration. + Synthetic data generation for research. * **Data Science and Machine Learning Methods in social sciences**. + AI and machine learning applications. + Causal inference with observational data. + Large Language Models (LLMs) and generative AI applications. + Sentiment, topic, and narrative analysis. + Data validation, quality and reproducibility. * **Applications in Economics and Social Sciences**. + eWOM and social media marketing. + Business analytics and digital marketing. + Data-driven innovation and competitiveness. + Data economy, governance and regulation. + Digital platforms and market structures. + e-Government and data-driven policy. + Economic inequality in the data economy. The Scientific Committee is particularly interested in receiving submissions that showcase applied and empirical research of significant interest to scholars of the social sciences. The CARMA 2026 conference will be held on 1 – 3 July 2026 at the Faculty of Business Administration and Management of the Universitat Politècnica de València (UPV), which has been recently ranked as the best technical university in Spain by the *Academic Ranking of World Universities* (ARWU) 2025.

# Causal inference, time and observation plans in the social sciences. This paper first discusses the role of time in causal inferences in the social sciences. It then compares in detail how panel and event history observation designs affect causal analysis. It shows that the collection of event history data is an extremely useful approach for uncovering causal relationships or mapping out systems of causal relations. It concludes that event history data provide an optimal basis for a causal understanding of social processes because they allow the social researcher to relate the change in future outcomes to conditions in the past at each point in time. ### Causal inference for time series analysis: problems, methods and evaluation. # Causal Inference in the Social Sciences. Annual Review of Statistics and Its Application. April2024 Vol. 11 Pages 123–152. Knowledge of causal effects is of great importance to decision makers in a wide variety of settings. In many cases, however, these causal effects are not known to the decision makers and need to be estimated from data. This fundamental problem has been known and studied for many years in many disciplines. In the past thirty years, however, the amount of empirical as well as methodological research in this area has increased dramatically, and so has its scope. It has become more interdisciplinary, and the focus has been more specifically on methods for credibly estimating causal effects in a wide range of both experimental and observational settings. This work has greatly impacted empirical work in the social and biomedical sciences. In this article, I review some of this work and discuss open questions.
